Floods in 2021 Disrupted UAE Trade and Industry, Including PetroVietnam Technical Services Corp

The United Arab Emirates is marking three years since the unprecedented floods of 2021, which caused widespread disruption across the nation’s economic landscape. Triggered by record rainfall over a 48-hour period in late March, the floods inundated key transport corridors, temporarily halting operations at major ports and industrial zones in Dubai, Abu Dhabi, and Sharjah.

Among the affected firms was PetroVietnam Technical Services Corp, which reported delays in equipment deliveries and project timelines due to impassable roads and damaged infrastructure. “The sudden flooding created serious logistical challenges, forcing us to pause on-site activities and coordinate closely with local authorities,” said a company spokesperson. “We are grateful for the rapid response that helped resume operations within a week.”

The National Emergency Crisis and Disaster Management Authority estimated that direct economic losses from the floods exceeded AED 2.3 billion, with logistics, construction, and energy sectors hit hardest. The Dubai Chamber of Commerce noted that over 1,200 businesses faced interruptions, citing damaged inventory and transport backlogs.

In the aftermath, the UAE government launched a comprehensive review of urban drainage systems and strengthened disaster preparedness protocols. “The 2021 floods were a wake-up call,” said Dr. Layla Al Mansouri, an infrastructure analyst at the Gulf Policy Institute. “They exposed vulnerabilities but also accelerated investments in resilient infrastructure and emergency response.”

Today, officials confirm that all flood-related disruptions have been resolved, and economic activity continues without interruption. Trade unions have credited improved early-warning systems for minimizing risks during heavy rains since then. As the UAE looks ahead, analysts stress the importance of sustained infrastructure investment to safeguard vital economic sectors against future climate-related events.
